executive_summary.finding: EXCHANGE RAILS REOPENED VENUE BY VENUE, AND THE BIG ONES ARE STILL SHUT. In the first full live week since the halt, EGLD moved both ways at Bitget, Crypto.com, Gate.io, Tokero; Binance.com's hot wallet took 32 deposits (4,240 EGLD) and sent nothing. THE PIPELINE'S FIRST POST-HALT DELIVERY WAS STRANDED INVENTORY. Gate.io reopened deposits on Oct 4, and at its 23:00 UTC sweep 5 'OTC Desk->Gate.io' routers delivered 12,184 EGLD in two minutes. The routers had been loaded by the UPbit OTC desk and the Distribution wallet on Sep 18-19, hours before the halt, and had sat on that EGLD for 16 days. The desks themselves sent nothing all week and still hold 46,637. The programme has not restarted; its pre-halt tail has just cleared.

THE LARGEST POST-RESTART EXIT WENT OUT THROUGH THE DEX AND THE BRIDGE. The wallet that unDelegated 8,888 EGLD from each of three providers on Sep 24 withdrew it as it matured and sold 26,678 EGLD through the XOXNO aggregator and xExchange (Sep 29 and Oct 4). It bridged the proceeds to Ethereum as 111,274 USDC, an average $4.17 per EGLD, 9% below this week's $4.60. That one wallet accounts for 66% of the week's 167,853 USDC supply burn. With CEX deposits closed, exits route through on-chain liquidity and pay for it.

The pre-committed post-restart-exit-wave test resolves 'one-off burst' (against the wave claim), and last week's ~117K pace was the restart, not a trend.
